proposed.sourceName: Darul Iftaa, Jaamia Madinatul Uloom (Trinidad) — 'Is Mono and di-glycerides (E471) permissible?' (Mufti Arshad Ali)
proposed.paraphrase: A Hanafi Darul Iftaa fatwa holding that E471 is permissible only when plant-derived; animal-derived is impermissible unless the animal was slaughtered per Islamic law. It instructs Muslims to avoid products with mono/diglycerides unless labeled 100% vegetable and to verify unlisted sources — so the strict Hanafi reading avoids undisclosed-origin E471.

proposed.sourceName: American Halal Foundation (AHF) — 'Are Mono Diglycerides Halal?' (Azmi Anees)
proposed.paraphrase: AHF notes pork-derived mono/diglycerides remain haram even under the Hanafi view because the transformation (istihalah) is not considered complete, and non-zabiha beef is likewise not halal; it advises avoiding E471 unless labeled vegetable or halal-certified. For undisclosed origin the strict Hanafi position therefore avoids it.

researcherNote: E471 seeded hanafiStrict = grade 4 (Questionable — widely avoided). Even the Hanafi istihalah latitude does NOT rescue undisclosed E471, because pork-derived mono/diglycerides are held to be incompletely transformed (still haram) and non-zabiha beef is impermissible — so the strict Hanafi position avoids. Primary source is itself a Hanafi Darul Iftaa fatwa; AHF independently confirms the Hanafi-specific point. Two independent tier-1 sources. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01.
